cases.name: Madison Renee "Flo" Crowe
cases.about: Her obituary said, "At a young age, Madison had a love for soccer, and quickly became an undaunted, fierce competitor known as “Mad –Flo” and eventually was just known as Flo Crowe. Flo was a bright student in school, where she had a love for creative writing. Even though she just started her sophomore year at Weir High School, she already had a goal in mind to one day be an accomplished physical therapist. Her hardworking determination also carried over to the soccer fields. Flo, by nature, could at times be a little quirky and clumsy tripping over the air, but this did not limit her success on-field due to the extra effort she displayed daily being the hardest worker on the field. She has worked on her game since she was in the U8 Rec and travel teams with the Tri-State United Soccer League, and she is currently a member of the Weir High School Soccer Team. Flo loved to spend time with her best friend and step- sister Jessie. They were like twins; inseparable. If they could not be together, they would be face timing each other. They loved to go over Nana’s and Pap’s house, spend time on the deck, and swim in their pool. Flo also enjoyed going to Subway with Nana for her favorite Buffalo Chicken sub."

cases.name: Melissa Anne Roy Rowland
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Melissa grew up in Weirton, WV, and graduated from Weir High School in 1999. After high school, she worked as a nurse aide on the fifth floor at Trinity Hospital for 15 years. Wanting to better herself, she enrolled in college and studied pharmacy at Penn Foster and became a certified pharmacy technician. Melissa was also formerly employed at Cigna and was currently employed as a Benefit Verification Specialist for Connective RX, in Bridgeville, Pa. In her free time, Melissa would always be there for others, constantly running and caring for her children. She loved decorating her home and making things with her Cricut. She loved traveling to Hilton Head with her family and always dreamed about retiring in the Carolina’s. Melissa always wore her flip flops year-round. She and her husband Chad also loved to go out to eat and try new restaurants. Wings were her favorite. They also shared their love for Hockey and would cheer for the Pittsburgh Penguins. But nothing compared to the unconditional love she had for her family. She cherished the times watching them play soccer, attending their school activities, or just having a movie night at home."

cases.name: Jordan Nicole Bettino
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "A graduate of Weir High School in the class of 2017, Jordan was currently furthering her education at West Virginia Northern Community College. Her dream was to embark on a career in the medical field, inspired by her innate desire to help and care for others.

Jordan’s life was a testament to her compassion and kindness. Known for her heart of gold, she would go to great lengths to assist anyone in need. Her children, Armani Edward, age 6, and Aniya Brooklynn Bettino, age 5, were the center of her universe. She cherished her time with them and extended her nurturing spirit to her niece and nephew, Aiden Bettino and Iris Bailey, often organizing spa days at home filled with laughter, and soothing music.

Her friends saw her as their rock, always present and supportive during times of need. Jordan nourished her faith at the Family of God Church."

cases.name: Zoe Eleni Antoniou
cases.about:
Her mother Jennifer Stevens said), "I know Zoe was just love and light and joy,” Stevens said. “She loved and she loved big, and if you had kids, she loved them ever bigger. She put everybody’s needs before her own. … She always wanted to do good.”

Stevens shared stories about Antoniou and invited others to do the same. Friends of Antoniou recalled her personality, as well as the origin of a photo with Antoniou and her friends on it that they turned into a T-Shirt, captioned with “Until we meet again sis.”

Her father, Jimmy Antoniou, said his daughter was “a bright light to a lot of us. … She was strong, and she wasn’t afraid to fight.”
